title: Purple, a letter Q and a phone on its side
label: Brand gallery
lede: Quibi’s identity was built in a little over a year: a round, heavy wordmark, a bright violet, and a Q whose tail doubled as a speech bubble. The marks survive in the archive. Beside them sit portraits of the two people behind the company and our own drawings in the same spirit.

archive.caption: The first wordmark, in black, from the holding page that went up when the name was announced.
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of quibi.com. Shown for commentary; the Quibi wordmark belongs to its owner.

archive.caption: The launch logo: a white Q mark and wordmark over video, enlarged from the home page header.
archive.alt: Quibi logo in white on a dark background
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of quibi.com. Shown for commentary; the Quibi logo belongs to its owner.

archive.caption: The home page in its last month of service, with the app shown on a phone.
archive.alt: Quibi home page in November 2020 showing a phone and the words Quick Bites, Big Stories
archive.credit: Internet Archive capture of quibi.com. Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: Jeffrey Katzenberg, Quibi’s founder and chairman, photographed in 2014 while chief executive of DreamWorks Animation.
archive.alt: Jeffrey Katzenberg speaking at an event in 2014
archive.credit: Photo: Gage Skidmore, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jeffrey_Katzenberg_%2814513937721%29.jpg), CC BY-SA 2.0.

archive.caption: Meg Whitman, Quibi’s chief executive, in her official portrait as United States ambassador to Kenya.
archive.credit: Photo: United States Department of State, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Meg_Whitman,_U.S._Ambassador.jpg), public domain.

drawings.title: The turn.
drawings.caption: A phone between portrait and landscape. Turnstyle was the feature Quibi built its shows around.[^26]

drawings.title: One scene, two frames.
drawings.caption: Every show was delivered in both orientations and kept in sync by its audio track.[^26]
